items.title: Section: Benefiting Beings in Five Concrete Ways — Teaching Genuinely Right Livelihood First, With Its Own Five Noble Benefits

items.zh: 又諸菩薩由五種相，於諸有情能作一切饒益之事。何等為五？一者、說授正命以為饒益；二者、於不隨順能引義利所作事業，說授隨順以為饒益；三者、無依無怙、有苦有貧，善能為彼作依怙等以為饒益；四者、說授能往善趣之道以為饒益；五者、說授三乘以為饒益。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas, through five marks, are able to perform every kind of beneficial deed for sentient beings. What are these five? First, teaching genuinely right livelihood as a benefit. Second, for occupations that fail to produce genuine benefit, teaching occupations that do, as a benefit. Third, for beings with no refuge and no support, suffering and impoverished, skilfully becoming their refuge and support as a benefit. Fourth, teaching the path leading towards a favourable rebirth as a benefit. Fifth, teaching the three vehicles as a benefit.

items.title: Section: Repaying Kindness in Five Ways — Inviting Others Into One's Own Practice, and Encouraging Devotion to the Teaching Itself

items.zh: 又諸菩薩由五種相，於其有恩諸有情所現前酬報。何等為五？一者、安處有情，令學己德；二者、方便安處，令學他德；三者、無依無怙、有苦有貧，隨力隨能作依怙等；四者、勸令供養諸佛如來；五者、令於如來所說正法受持、讀誦、書寫、供養。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas, through five marks, directly repay beings who have shown them kindness. What are these five? First, settling such beings well and having them train in the bodhisattva's own virtues. Second, skilfully settling them instead so that they train in virtues suited to them. Third, for such beings who are without refuge or support, suffering, and impoverished, becoming their refuge and support according to one's own strength and ability. Fourth, encouraging them to make offerings to the buddhas and tathāgatas. Fifth, having them receive, recite, copy, and revere the true teaching spoken by the Tathāgata.

items.title: Section: Five Occasions a Bodhisattva Always Rejoices In — Living in a Buddha's Own Age, and Twenty-Seven Skilful Means of Maturing Beings

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於五種處常當欣讚。何等為五？一者、值佛出世，常得承事；二者、於諸佛所，常聞六種波羅蜜多菩薩藏法；三者、於一切種成熟有情，常有勢力；四者、能於無上正等菩提堪任速證；五者、證菩提已，諸弟子眾常和無諍。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas should constantly delight in and praise five circumstances. What are these five? First, encountering a buddha's appearance in the world and constantly being able to serve that buddha. Second, constantly hearing, in the presence of every buddha, the six perfections and the bodhisattva canon's own teaching. Third, constantly possessing genuine power to mature beings through every kind of means. Fourth, being genuinely capable of swiftly attaining supreme, correct awakening. Fifth, having attained awakening, presiding over disciples who remain constantly harmonious and free of dispute.

items.title: Section: Effort That Is Never Wasted — Closing the First Summary Verse's Seven Qualities Entirely

items.zh: 又諸菩薩由五因緣，於諸有情能作不虛饒益加行。何等為五？謂諸菩薩，於諸有情先欲求作利益安樂，於諸有情利益安樂如實了知，無顛倒覺。如是一切，如前供養親近無量品中所說，應知其相。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas, through five causes and conditions, are able to bring about genuine, never-wasted benefit for sentient beings through their own effort. What are these five? Bodhisattvas who wish, beforehand, to bring benefit and ease to beings; who correctly and thoroughly know, without any distorted understanding, what genuinely constitutes that benefit and ease for beings. All of this, exactly as already explained in the earlier chapter on venerating the three jewels, approaching good friends, and cultivating the immeasurables, should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: The Second Summary Verse Opens — Six Categories, Beginning With Five Kinds of Correct, Undistorted Effort Matched to Each Stage of the Path

items.zh: 復次，嗢拕南曰：無顛倒加行、退墮、與勝進、相似、實功德、善調伏有情。謂諸菩薩有五加行，當知普攝一切菩薩無倒加行。何等為五？一、隨護加行，二、無罪加行，三、思擇力加行，四、清淨增上意樂加行，五、墮決定加行。
items.en: Furthermore, a summary verse states: "Undistorted effort; regression and genuine advancement; resemblance and genuine merit; skilfully taming beings." One should understand that bodhisattvas have five kinds of effort that universally encompass every bodhisattva's undistorted effort. What are these five? First, protective effort; second, faultless effort; third, the effort of investigative power; fourth, the effort of pure, excellent aspiration; fifth, the effort of falling into certainty.

items.title: Section: Protective Effort Opens — Named in Five Kinds

items.zh: 云何菩薩隨護加行？當知此復略有五種。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's protective effort? One should understand that this, in brief outline, further divides into five kinds.

items.title: Section: Sustaining Innate Wisdom, and Sustaining Correct Mindfulness

items.zh: 一者、隨護聰叡。謂由俱生智速疾攝法。二者、隨護正念。謂由此正念，隨所攝法持令不忘。
items.en:
First, sustaining innate wisdom. This means that, through innate wisdom, one swiftly grasps the teaching.
Commentary: Regarding "sustaining innate wisdom" and the like — keen hearing and clear sight are called being sharp; deep understanding is called being wise. The Compendium of Determinations, Differing Gateways explains that being sharp means being joined with wisdom that has been cultivated through effort, while being wise means being joined with wisdom that is innate and inborn — or, alternatively, the reverse assignment is also given. Here the passage speaks specifically in terms of wisdom joined with what is innate, explaining the name accordingly, which is why it says wisdom that is innate and inborn swiftly grasps the teaching.
Second, sustaining correct mindfulness. This means that, through this correct mindfulness, whatever teaching has been grasped is retained without being forgotten.

items.title: Section: Sustaining Correct Understanding, Guarding the Wisdom Already Gained From Both Sides

items.zh: 三者、隨護正智。謂由此正智，於所持法善觀察義，正慧通達。遠離隨順聰叡正念覺慧退分諸因緣故，習近隨順住分、勝分諸因緣故。
items.en:
Third, sustaining correct understanding. This means that, through this correct understanding, one skilfully examines the meaning of whatever teaching has been retained, and correct wisdom penetrates it. One thereby stays free of whatever conditions would cause the wisdom joined with sharpness and correct mindfulness to regress, and draws close to whatever conditions would let that same wisdom remain stable and continue advancing.
Commentary: Regarding "staying free of whatever conditions would cause the wisdom joined with sharpness and correct mindfulness to regress" and the like — the wisdom joined with sharpness and with correct mindfulness is here called the wisdom of sharpness and correct mindfulness. Wherever conditions exist that would incline that wisdom towards regression, correct understanding is what allows one to stay free of them; wherever conditions exist that would let that wisdom remain stable or continue advancing, correct understanding is what allows one to draw close to them. The conditions of regression and of advancement referred to here should be understood exactly as explained below, in the sections on conditions favouring regression and conditions favouring advancement.

items.title: Section: Guarding One's Own Mind and Guarding the Minds of Others — Protective Effort Closes in Full

items.zh: 四者、隨護自心。能善防守諸根門故。五者、隨護他心。能於他心正隨轉故。
items.en:
Fourth, guarding one's own mind. This means being able to skilfully guard the doors of the sense faculties.
Fifth, guarding the minds of others. This means being able to cause the minds of others to turn correctly and follow along.

items.zh: 云何菩薩無罪加行？謂諸菩薩，於諸善法無倒熾然，無量無間迴向菩提。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's faultless effort? It means that bodhisattvas, with respect to every wholesome teaching, undistortedly and with blazing intensity, dedicate immeasurable, uninterrupted cultivation towards awakening.

items.title: Section: The Effort of Investigative Power, Belonging to the Stage of Resolute Practice

items.zh: 云何菩薩思擇力加行？謂諸菩薩，即此一切在勝解行地，應知其相。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's effort of investigative power? It means that this entire cultivation, in bodhisattvas who are in the stage of resolute practice, should be understood to take on its own particular character there.

items.title: Section: The Effort of Pure, Excellent Aspiration, Belonging to Grounds One Through Seven

items.zh: 云何菩薩清淨增上意樂加行？謂諸菩薩，即此一切在淨勝意樂地及行正行地，應知其相。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's effort of pure, excellent aspiration? It means that this entire cultivation, in bodhisattvas who are in the ground of pure, excellent aspiration and the ground of genuinely correct practice, should be understood to take on its own particular character there.
Commentary: Regarding "the ground of pure, excellent aspiration and the ground of genuinely correct practice" — the abode of utmost joy is called the ground of pure, excellent aspiration; the abode of excellent moral discipline, the abode of excellent mind, the three abodes of excellent wisdom, and the abode with effort and application yet already free of marks are together called the ground of genuinely correct practice. This is as explained in the chapter on the grounds.

items.title: Section: The Effort of Falling Into Certainty, Belonging to Grounds Eight Through Ten

items.zh: 云何菩薩墮決定加行？謂諸菩薩，即此一切在決定地、決定行地、到究竟地，應知其相。
items.en:
What is a bodhisattva's effort of falling into certainty? It means that this entire cultivation, in bodhisattvas who are in the ground of certainty, the ground of certain conduct, and the ground of arrival at the ultimate, should be understood to take on its own particular character there.
Commentary: Regarding "the ground of certainty, the ground of certain conduct, and the ground of arrival at the ultimate" — the abode without effort, without application, already abiding in the mark-free realm is called the ground of certainty, since bodhisattvas at this ground have fallen into the third kind of certainty; the abode of unobstructed understanding is called the ground of certain conduct; the abode of the bodhisattva of supreme, complete accomplishment is called the ground of arrival at the ultimate. This too is as explained in the chapter on the grounds.

items.title: Section: The Conclusion — Five Kinds of Effort Universally Encompass All Undistorted Effort

items.zh: 如是五種菩薩加行，普攝一切無倒加行。
items.en: Such are the five kinds of bodhisattva effort, which universally encompass every kind of undistorted effort.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩順退分法，當知有五。何等為五？一者、不敬正法及說法師。二者、放逸懈怠。三者、於諸煩惱親近執著。四者、於諸惡行親近執著。五者、與餘菩薩校量勝劣，起增上慢；及於法顛倒，起增上慢。
items.en: Furthermore, one should understand that bodhisattvas have five conditions favouring regression. What are these five? First, disrespecting the true teaching and the teachers who expound it. Second, heedlessness and laziness. Third, drawing close to and clinging to one's own afflictions. Fourth, drawing close to and clinging to unwholesome conduct. Fifth, comparing oneself against other bodhisattvas to claim superiority, giving rise to arrogance; and holding a distorted view of the teaching, likewise giving rise to arrogance.

items.title: Section: Five Conditions Favouring Advancement — the Exact Mirror of Regression

items.zh: 又諸菩薩順勝分法，當知有五。何等為五？謂與前五黑品諸法次第相違，應知其相。
items.en: Furthermore, one should understand that bodhisattvas have five conditions favouring advancement. What are these five? One should understand that their character is, point by point, the exact reverse of the five preceding conditions belonging to the dark class of teachings just explained.

items.title: Section: Counterfeit Merit Opens — Abandoning the Vicious, and Feigning Dignified Deportment

items.zh: 又諸菩薩略有五種相似功德，當知實是菩薩過失。何等為五？一者、於其暴惡毀犯淨戒諸有情所，由是因緣作不饒益；二者、詐現種種具足威儀；
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas have, in brief, five kinds of counterfeit merit that one should understand to actually be faults. What are these five? First, refusing to benefit beings who are vicious and have violated pure precepts, using this very circumstance as the pretext. Second, feigning a complete and elaborate display of dignified deportment.
Commentary: Regarding "refusing to benefit beings who are vicious and have violated pure precepts, using this very circumstance as the pretext" — the chapter on moral discipline explains that harbouring resentment or harbouring anger and distress towards beings who are vicious and have violated the precepts, and on the pretext of their viciousness and violation, contriving to abandon them and refuse to benefit them, constitutes a transgression, a violation, indeed a defiled transgression. Its meaning should be understood accordingly.
Commentary: Regarding "feigning a complete and elaborate display of dignified deportment" — this means constantly feigning, in order to deceive others, faculties that show no agitation, no movement, and complete tranquility, so that others believe one to be virtuous and are moved to make offerings or perform service. This should be understood as explained in the Stage of Disciples.

items.title: Section: Counterfeit Merit Continues — Worldly Cleverness, Tainted Giving, and Spreading Counterfeit Teaching

items.zh: 三者、於順世間文詞、呪術、外道書論相應法中，得預智者、聰叡者數；四者、修行有罪施等善行；五者、宣說建立像似正法，廣令流布。
items.en: Third, being counted among the wise and the clever specifically for teachings concordant with worldly rhetoric, incantations, and the treatises of non-Buddhist schools. Fourth, practising giving and similar wholesome conduct while it is still tainted by fault. Fifth, preaching and establishing a counterfeit version of the true teaching and causing it to spread widely.

blocks.text: A long day of short lists. Read them as a portrait: how a bodhisattva helps, how they protect their own practice, what makes practice decline or grow, and what only looks like virtue.

"First, teaching right livelihood as a benefit." Master Cháng Bǎi: a layperson's occupation must accord with the Buddhist principle of cause and effect. Venerable Miào Jìng, mimicking the worldly attitude: "if one lie earned a hundred thousand dollars, of course I'd tell it."

"First, settling beings so they train in the bodhisattva's own virtues." Master Cháng Bǎi: mainly teaching them to walk the bodhisattva path together. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is the gathering-in of shared conduct.
Master Cháng Bǎi: all disciples practise the six harmonies, always united and free of dispute. (The Chinese 欣讚 is "delight and praise"; Ru-Yi gives only "delight".)
Venerable Miào Jìng: doing a little good with a grasping mind earns human or divine merit, and when it is spent, all that good comes to zero.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the effort of investigative power belongs to bodhisattvas before the grounds; the effort of falling into certainty to the eighth, ninth, and tenth grounds.

Sustaining innate wisdom, correct mindfulness, correct understanding, one's own mind, and others' minds. Venerable Miào Jìng: these five teach the order and method of learning the Dharma. Master Cháng Bǎi: at the start of practice, first protect yourself and become pure; only then can you guide beings.

Venerable Miào Jìng: the house is your mind, the snake its afflictions; at the stage of resolute practice one can tame the snake so it does not move. Master Cháng Bǎi: on the first ground afflictions can be cut, so aspiration is "pure"; "fall into certainty" means enter irreversible effort; only from the eighth ground is no intention needed.

"Second, heedlessness and laziness." Venerable Miào Jìng: laziness is failing to cultivate good; heedlessness is failing to cut off evil. And drawing close to afflictions: "The poisonous snake is my good friend, I want to be with it always."

"Bodhisattvas have five kinds of counterfeit merit that should be understood to actually be faults." Master Cháng Bǎi: they look like merit but are faults. Turning harshly away from the vicious looks righteous, but compassion is lost.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a doctorate in literature or a Nobel Prize: in the Dharma such worldly accomplishments are only counterfeit merit. Venerable Miào Jìng: coming into the Dharma, yet studying worldly knowledge instead.
Counterfeit merit is a useful mirror. Each of us can ask which of our good qualities is real and which is partly for show.

quiz.q: What is the first of five ways a bodhisattva benefits beings?
quiz.why: "First, teaching right livelihood as a benefit." Master Cháng Bǎi: a layperson's occupation must accord with the Buddhist principle of cause and effect. Venerable Miào Jìng mimics the worldly attitude: if one lie earned a hundred thousand dollars, of course I'd tell it.

quiz.q: What is the first way a bodhisattva repays those who were kind?
options: settling them to train in the bodhisattva's own virtues
quiz.why: "First, settling beings so they train in the bodhisattva's own virtues." Master Cháng Bǎi: mainly teaching them to walk the bodhisattva path together. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is the gathering-in of shared conduct.

quiz.q: On "never-wasted beneficial effort," what example does Venerable Miào Jìng give of "wasted"?
options: doing good with a grasping mind earns human or divine merit — once used up, it all comes to nothing
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: doing a little good with a grasping mind earns human or divine merit — and when it's spent, all that good comes to zero. Master Cháng Bǎi: never wasting the beneficial effort one makes.

quiz.q: What are the five kinds of protective effort?
options: sustaining innate wisdom, mindfulness, correct understanding, one's own mind, others' minds
quiz.why: Sustaining innate wisdom, correct mindfulness, correct understanding, one's own mind, and others' minds. Venerable Miào Jìng: these five teach the order and method of learning the dharma.

quiz.q: On the order of guarding one's own mind and others', what does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: first guard yourself and become pure, then you can guide beings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: at the start of practice, first protect yourself and become pure; only then can you guide beings. The English note's claim that there is no order contradicts this.

quiz.q: Investigative effort belongs to the stage of resolute practice. How do the lectures describe this stage?
options: Miào Jìng: the house is the mind, the snake affliction — this stage can tame the snake; Cháng Bǎi: calming accomplished gives the mind power ("resolute"); constant practice turning defiled to pure is "practice"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the house is your mind, the snake its afflictions — in the stage of resolute practice one can tame the snake so it doesn't move. Master Cháng Bǎi: calming accomplished, the mind has strength — "resolute"; constantly practising calm and insight, gradually turning defilement into purity — "practice."

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain "falling" in "falling into certainty," and why only from the eighth ground?
options: both: "fall" means enter — entering irreversible effort; before the eighth ground, effort is still needed, so not yet "certain"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "fall" means enter — entering irreversible effort; before that, intentional effort is still needed, so it's not "certain." Venerable Miào Jìng: only from the eighth ground is no intention required; "fall" is read as "enter."

quiz.q: What is the second of five conditions favouring regression?
quiz.why: "Second, heedlessness and laziness." Venerable Miào Jìng: laziness is failing to cultivate good; heedlessness is failing to cut off evil.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say a bodhisattva's "counterfeit merit" really is?
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas have five kinds of counterfeit merit that should be understood to actually be faults." Master Cháng Bǎi: they look like merit but are faults.

quiz.q: The third counterfeit — counted wise for worldly rhetoric and outsider treatises. What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: having a literature PhD or a Nobel Prize — in the dharma such worldly things are only counterfeit merit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having or about to have a doctorate in literature or a Nobel Prize — in the dharma such worldly accomplishments are only counterfeit merit. Venerable Miào Jìng: coming into the dharma, yet studying worldly knowledge instead.
